_: Ways between locations that data/exits.json does not give, kept by hand. Read by server/travel.py. 'doors' overrides exits.json for one door (outzones side a or b) of one location: the target, and why it is believed. 'walk_in' lists cells that lead somewhere although the location file has no zone on them, so the client never opens its exit window there; the server moves the player once their walk ends on one (server.py, Session.arm_passage). None are listed now -- the Nubian mine's mouth and its EXIT sign, the two there were, became the quests below -- and the mechanism stays for the next place that needs one (server/test_walk_in.py runs it on a table of its own, LAVA_PASSAGES). 'quest' lists the ways a quest of an inhabitant of the location takes a player: taken, it sits in the journal like any quest, and handed in to the same inhabitant it moves him there (server.py, Session.hand_in_way) -- nothing paid, nothing counted against the day; its cells are where the file draws that way, beside which a player coming the other way arrives (travel.door_arrival). A quest named here is refused, taken or handed in, in a location with no row for it. Cells are [x, y] of the location's own grid. Every row says whether it is RECOVERED (the client's files show it) or DESIGNED (ours, because what the original did there is lost with the serverdata node).
